claims.text: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy is FCC-structured after thermomechanical processing.
The equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after the same thermomechanical treatment.
Differences in mechanical behavior among the quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys stem from variations in local lattice distortion.
Differences in mechanical behavior among the alloys stem from variations in short-range ordering.
Local lattice distortion and short-range order modulate dislocation mobility during deformation.
The five-element combination in equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni produces an optimal level of local lattice distortion.
The five-element combination promotes beneficial short-range-order clusters.
The proposed short-range-order clusters impede dislocation motion in a balanced manner.
Balanced impediment of dislocation motion enhances strain hardening in the quinary alloy.
Balanced impediment of dislocation motion enhances ductility in the quinary alloy.
Removing one or two elements changes atomic-size mismatch and chemical interactions and disrupts the balance of dislocation barriers.
Reduced-element alloys can have either insufficient or excessive barriers to dislocation motion.
Changes in these barriers alter dislocation nucleation, mobility, and interaction, thereby changing strain hardening and failure behavior.
Relative to the quinary baseline, quaternary and especially ternary subsets will have lower work-hardening rates.
The quaternary and ternary subsets will have yield strengths different from the quinary baseline.
The quinary alloy will exhibit greater ductility and a more gradual strain-hardening response than the subsets.
The controlled comparison uses room-temperature tensile tests at a common strain rate on single-phase FCC specimens with similar grain sizes and nominally identical thermomechanical histories.
Minor grain-size variations or residual-stress differences may also influence mechanical performance.

The hypothesis is falsified if the quinary alloy lacks statistically significant differences in both short-range-order density and local lattice distortion relative to the subsets, or if those mediators fail to correlate with work hardening and ductility.
